title: Dreamland's decoration, mixed crowd, breakfast dances and her clothes
summary: At Bottoms's Dreamland she earned $17.50; gamblers, pimps, elites, whites and Blacks came; she started wearing smart clothes, including Turkish bloomers, with Carrie Ward.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Now, after I -- well, then from the De Luxe I went across to Dreamland, and there's where Mr. Bottoms, Bill Bottoms, who turned out to be Joe Louis's dietician, he owned the Dreamland.
Yes.

Across the street. And he used to -- he had different people out trying to get me to work for him. And I got $17.50 a week. Oh, that was money, $17.50, and there's where I really made money, because Dan Gaines and most of these fellows were gamblers, now, over to Dreamland --
Yes.
-- were the gamblers and the pimps and everybody came, white and colored.
Dreamland --
Now, there's where there was decoration.
Yeah. That's the one I had a picture of.
Yeah. Had the big --
With the balcony and the bandstand.
That's where Lil and them sat up on the balcony.
Right.
And under the balcony were tables, too, and then there was a big square glass and the dance floor.
Uh-huh.
See? And that's where -- and I think Mr. Bottoms and them were the first ones to start having the breakfast dances.
Uh-huh.
See, you'd start -- people would come in for breakfast dances. Excuse me. And then --
At Dreamland you had a mixed clientele.
Oh, very much so.
Uh-huh.
Very much so, black and white. Now that was where --
Did you have the pickpockets and that element there?
Everybody came, but it wasn't exclusively the pickpockets and the sporting people.
Uh-huh.
But they came and the pickpockets didn't bother anybody. They came to enjoy themselves, and they did.

They didn't bother anybody. They didn't pick anybody's pocket or anything like that. It was all types of people, and some of our elite, the Chicago elite, came, too. They used to -- oh, and talk about smart. Now, there's where I started putting on clothes.
Uh-huh.

Had to dress. And a friend of mine, Carrie Ward, Carrie Mae Ward, she was a friend of mine and she was crazy about good clothes. And she used to go downtown and pick out the smartest clothes. I was the first one started wearing -- you know, like the Turks wear, like the big bloomers at the legs, like the --
Oh, yes.
I was the first one to wear those kind of clothes.
